0.content:
Donatello, Chevreuse's father, was a Garde praised by everyone as upright. He worked from early morning to late night and came home with sweets and apologies. During a major case he leaked secret intelligence to the press, hoping the public interest would help catch the criminal. His colleagues searched the house, a court convicted him, and he was exiled to the Fortress of Meropide. His wife and daughter fell into poverty in the Fleuve Cendre, where his former colleagues quietly helped them and campaigned so he would not be punished further. After serving his sentence he joined the Special Patrol and trained Chevreuse harshly. She passed every trial, including swims in freezing winter seas, and he decided she was more fit to uphold justice than he was.

When she went before the Patrol Captain's hearing to take over the post, Donatello proofread her statement so it would give the Maison Gardiennage the "decent" account it needed. She ended by stating that his conviction was correct. Her lessons from him: the law's worst insult is a criminal walking free, the Maison's dignity matters less than the city's safety, and law enforcers must govern themselves by their own conception of justice. His present status is not stated.

1.content:
Vice Captain Grizzetti of the Special Patrol had been close to Donatello and looked after Chevreuse, who called him "Uncle Grizzetti". Although she topped her class, he kept her off field missions because her idea of justice was "an eye for an eye". Short-handed one stormy night, he finally took her on a hunt for a notorious gang. A hidden shooter killed him. Chevreuse shot back at the muzzle flash, then stood over the wounded killer, alone in the rain, with her musket aimed between his eyes. She lowered it and arrested him, and shot him in the right leg when he tried to flee. Afterwards she found a Pyro Vision hanging from the stock.

She rarely talks about this. Publicly she says the Patrol's authority comes from law and justice, so talking about Visions only causes misunderstandings. Friends know the Vision feels like a burden to her. The story's moral is that the law's justice is decided by the courts, while her own justice is carried out by her alone.

2.comment: Chevreuse: Special Security and Surveillance Patrol
2.content:
The Special Security and Surveillance Patrol is a branch of the Maison Gardiennage that apprehends violent criminals the ordinary Gardes cannot handle. It does not do routine street patrols, investigates less than it arrests, and works with the Marechaussee Phantom. Members need not wear uniforms outside formal occasions or carry standard weapons. Under Chevreuse most carry muskets, refuse Gardemek support, and must also pass unarmed-combat standards. The Patrol accepts the descendants of disgraced criminals, and Chevreuse invites even serious felons to act as "special consultants", which the rest of the Maison Gardiennage resents. Her stock reply: "The greatest insult to the law is a criminal roaming free and unpunished."

Its reputation is fearsome; the Gardes' captain Grosrochard has written at least nine letters begging her to stop recruiting ex-burglars, street fighters and a would-be bank robber she caught herself. Members include Letellier, Turenna and Faderne. When a member dies on duty, the Patrol keeps their cap for their child. A covert officer once died leaving no picture of himself even for his family; each officer gave his son a gift, and Chevreuse gave her favourite novel.

3.content:
After her father's conviction Chevreuse and her mother lived in the Fleuve Cendre, the poor district beneath the Court of Fontaine. She worked for a kind shop owner while a neighbouring couple helped care for her ailing mother. The local children brought her their quarrels as a joke; she came back with legal books and a notebook and heard both sides properly, then personally saw her rulings carried out. She says growing up there showed her how much of Fontaine stays in shadow, and taught her many ways to make justice stick.

She still uses its networks. In the 4.3 film-festival case, when Paimon was surprised to see the Patrol's Captain there, she said simply that she grew up there. She paid the information broker Emerald for a lead, and questioned the bar owner Tetreaux.

4.content:
Chiori, the designer who owns Chioriya Boutique, is one of Chevreuse's closest working friends. Chiori's network has given the Patrol intelligence more than once. In return, Chevreuse turns a blind eye when Chiori throws someone out of her shop or drives off a malignant competitor. She notes that Chiori is always in the right and just doesn't bother explaining. Chiori finds working with her a cinch. It was Chiori who brought her into the 4.3 film.

In Chiori's Story Quest (4.5), Chevreuse explained that she often protects Chiori from the rich and powerful, and sometimes protects people from Chiori. When Chiori threw the designer Uther out of his own home, Chevreuse feigned ignorance. Afterwards she scolded Chiori for the anxiety her actions had caused. Chiori cheerfully pointed out that she had busted an underground factory and delivered the man responsible.

5.comment: Chevreuse: Roses and Muskets and the Rainbow Rose murder
5.content:
In the limited-time 4.3 event, Chiori recruited Chevreuse as a musket consultant for Xavier's film of the novel "The Two Musketeers", directed by Furina. When Kamisato Ayato withdrew, she took the lead role of the elder sister Tulipe opposite Ayaka's Iris. At the same time she was privately investigating a murder that copied the novel: a Rainbow Rose left on a victim from the Fleuve Cendre. With the Traveler's help, Emilie's analysis traced the rose to the novelist Baptiste, who confessed falsely.

The truth: twenty years earlier the investor Morris had an affair with a maid, Elisa, and later had her killed. Her two children, Baptiste and the film's prop manager Veronique, had killed the hired murderer and meant to kill Morris. Morris had also tried to sabotage the film. At the wrap party Chevreuse set a trap that frightened Morris into confessing. She aimed at him but did not fire, and blocked Veronique's shot at him with her musket. She arrested all three. She asked Wriothesley to make sure Morris did not live comfortably in Meropide, and to hand out the Steambird that would cast the siblings as heroes and Morris as the villain. Veronique told her that justice had not been served. Afterwards Chevreuse told the Traveler about her childhood by the sea. The film won the festival, and Ayaka invited her to Inazuma.

6.content: Emilie, the perfumer and forensic chemist, is a good friend Chevreuse met through work. Emilie can tell a suspect's perfume, the flowers they sent, even the soil they walked on, and Chevreuse says she has never been wrong. Their chats are lighter than their jobs. Chevreuse once described a novel about a perfumer who made scent from human tissue. Emilie doubted the scent would really be wonderful, while Chevreuse was busy working out the legal liabilities. Emilie also identified the Rainbow Rose in the 4.3 case (limited event).

7.comment: Chevreuse: Lyney, Lynette and the Imitation Sinthe case
7.content: Chevreuse once hired Lyney as a consultant to expose a murderer who used magic tricks; an author's novel about the case was held back for being too graphic. In the Detectives branch of Lynette's Hangout Event she brought him in again, as her "assistant", to investigate Imitation Sinthe smuggled into Fontaine. The trail ran to Pierre, a Fontaine Research Institute researcher secretly descended from the fallen Lefevere family, and his cat. She suspects the House of the Hearth's Harbinger ruined the Lefeveres but says she has no evidence and no wish to defend "such a despicable family". She welcomed Lynette to the team and, impressed, said she would recruit her if she thought Lynette would accept. Together they caught the smuggler Elodie Lefevere, a Lefevere plant inside the Gardes, and Chevreuse promised to find someone better to run the Humane Society.

8.comment: Chevreuse: Wriothesley and the Fortress of Meropide
8.content: Her father served time in the Fortress of Meropide, and many of her arrests end there. She values Wriothesley's work: criminals know Meropide is no place to grow old in, which helps her interrogations. He says inmates gain respect for the rules after meeting her Patrol. She sometimes sends him a "heads-up" about prisoners; he never promises anything, but he doesn't refuse. She hopes the people she sends there take their second chance. In 6.7 (limited event) she got the Duke's blessing and the Iudex's approval for well-behaved inmates to spend supervised time outside during the Fontinalia Festival.

9.content: She agrees with Neuvillette that justice must be free of personal feeling ("Those who break the law bear guilt. It's as simple as that."). Furina once ordered the Patrol to rehearse a ceremonial musketeer drill with special muskets; the idea died when no suitable music could be found. Furina later directed the 4.3 film Chevreuse starred in (limited event). In the 5.6 Whirling Waltz event (limited), her Patrol joined an operation Neuvillette and Wriothesley coordinated in a gray-market gambling case.

10.comment: Chevreuse: Navia, Clorinde and the Spina
10.content: Chevreuse remembers the stir the murder of Navia's father Callas caused in the Maison Gardiennage, and is glad the truth came out: "Justice may not always be swift, but it always prevails in the end." She trusts that the Champion Duelist Clorinde duels from her own sense of justice. Clorinde admires how Chevreuse fought off excessive-force lawsuits. In the 6.5 Nod-Krai operation (limited event), Navia ran the Spina's booth as Chevreuse's cover, with Clorinde as her bodyguard. The Spina supplied the manpower for the round-up.

11.comment: Chevreuse: The Nod-Krai Trade Expo operation
11.content:
In the limited-time 6.5 event, Chevreuse travelled to Nasha Town in Nod-Krai on official business. Gangs in Fontaine had been receiving unusually powerful weapons, and a leaked cargo manifest pointed to the Voynich Guild's Nod-Krai Trade Expo, a lawful black market whose one rule is no violence. Yelan of Liyue was hunting the same arms ring. After a negotiation at the Curatorium of Secrets, Nefer agreed they could act on any deal made outside the expo, as long as the Traveler took part. The pair baited the ring with weapons sold through Navia and Beidou. Chevreuse herded a fleeing agent with precise shots, wrecking a Guild signboard ("an unavoidable sacrifice"), while around twenty agents were taken.

The ring's leader, Sennedjem, had years earlier sold weapons designed by Ashvapati, a Kshahrewar researcher expelled from the Akademiya, to the enemies of the Eremite tribe that had sheltered them both, and the tribe was wiped out. Ashvapati had raised three surviving orphans and lured everyone to Nod-Krai for revenge. Chevreuse tried to talk him out of a suicidal barrage, which Beidou's ship turned into fireworks. She told him a public trial was more like real justice than an unremembered revenge killing. She took the arms dealers into custody. She did not charge Ashvapati, and Nefer dropped the claim for the signboard. She told him his crime was failing to use his knowledge to protect his people, and that his chance to atone was right in front of him.

12.content: Although her Patrol belongs to the Maison Gardiennage, Chevreuse rarely uses Gardemeks: they "would only get in the way of our bullets" and could be turned against her squad. (In her 5.7 Anecdote, her officers still complain that she uses Gardemeks to fire the signal flares in drills.) Grosrochard, captain of the Gardes, sends her pleading letters about her recruits. She worries about the growing number of injured Gardes and means to request better compensation for them.

13.content: During the limited-time 4.3 event, Chevreuse and Veronique taught Ayaka to handle prop muskets. Chevreuse then played Tulipe, the protective elder sister, to Ayaka's Iris. Furina rewrote the script to give the sisters equal weight. Chevreuse and the others praised Ayaka's real tears on camera. By the festival's end Ayaka counted her a new friend and invited her to Inazuma; Chevreuse said she would come when she had time.

14.content: The Special Patrol has a long friendship with the Melusines and often works with those in the Marechaussee Phantom on major cases. Chevreuse calls them kind, honest and reliable, is close to several including Sigewinne, and warns that anyone who slanders them will "find themselves looking down the barrels of our muskets". The Patrol has a Melusine cafeteria that serves buttered Tidalga.

15.comment: Chevreuse: Joint wargames with other nations
15.content: During the limited-time 4.7 event, Chevreuse and Grosrochard sent the Patrol officer Turenna to a joint wargame in Liyue. Chevreuse was delighted with the invitation, since both sides learn tactics and technology from these exchanges. In the limited-time 6.7 event Final Long-Range Sightlines, she co-ran a "Ballistic Wargame" at Lumidouce Harbor with Natlan's Chasca and Hedwig of the Knights of Favonius. It used observation grenades to train trajectory planning, and the Traveler served as a control group. Chevreuse and Chasca signed a "Joint Training Memorandum on Improving Shooter Effectiveness". Natlanese warriors would learn squad formations; Patrol shooters would be flown low by Qucusaurs to practise shooting at moving targets. Mondstadt would share the results. She gave up any thought of recruiting Chasca, as it would cost Natlan too much.

16.content: In the 6.7 Story Quest Sunny Summer Fontinalia (permanent, released with the limited event of the same name), at that year's Fontinalia Film Festival, Chevreuse greeted the returning Traveler with Chiori, having arranged festival leave for well-behaved Meropide inmates under Patrol supervision. She met Columbina, whom the Traveler introduced as a friend from Nod-Krai and who greeted people by punching their arms. Chevreuse read it as an odd "gesture of friendship". Her part in Xavier's new film shrank when he changed its direction, so she consulted on musket work and played a detective in Charlotte's crew's mystery film. She also lent her expertise on criminal investigation. Effects in one film were based on items the Patrol had confiscated.

17.content: The Steambird reporter Charlotte is "the type of reporter that really gives you a headache". She gets to major crime scenes first however well they are secured, and once wrote her article while detained as a suspect for half a month. Chevreuse keeps meaning to speak to her editor. Even so, she uses the press when it serves justice, as in the 4.3 case, and in 6.7 she played a detective opposite Charlotte on film, reassuring her that acting gets easier.

18.comment: Chevreuse: Chevreuse at festivals and events
18.content: In the limited Springtime Charms Lantern Rite (5.3), Chevreuse was in Liyue on compulsory leave. The Patrol had found she had not taken a single day off, and a Gestionnaire handed her a boat ticket. She loved the tea dim sum from Qiaoying Village, could not make a gift envelope look right, and asked the Traveler for help. Even on holiday she wondered whether her officers were keeping up their training. In the limited Whirling Waltz event (5.6) she took a captured criminal off Kinich's hands and thanked him and Cacucu for their "show-stopping performances".

key: Sin: The Kind that Doesn't Need to be Dealt With
19.content: On duty Chevreuse lives on grease and sugar, and keeps snacks in her uniform. She calls Feast-O's the best snack: portable and good with many sauces. On days off those "fat-inducing" foods become her worst enemy, and "absolving the world of their existence" (eating them) has its own pleasures. She will not eat raw food. Gifts of food get a sigh and a promise of extra training. Her birthday letters pair cake or movie snacks with 10 km runs, endurance sets or winter swims.

20.content: Chevreuse is a regular at Beaumont Workshop and buys the most expensive, advanced components for her musket. Freminet, who heard this, hopes to afford such parts for his Pers one day. Once they both reached for the last gadget in a shop; before she could let him have it, he ran out as if the Gardes were after him. In the 4.3 case she checked Beaumont Workshop and Leschots Clockwork Workshop for gun parts (limited event).
